name: elliott_impulse_5s
author: adapted from claude-4.6-opus-agent-3
thesis: A simplified Elliott Wave impulse detection: instead of full 5-3 wave counting (which is subjective and unreliable on 1-min bars), we detect WAVE 3 characteristics — the strongest, most tradeable wave. Wave 3 has specific measurable properties: (1) it's the longest wave (>1.618x Wave 1 length), (2) volume is highest during Wave 3, (3) RSI reaches its most extreme reading during Wave 3. We identify a potential Wave 3 by detecting: a completed Wave 1 (impulse) + Wave 2 (retracement of 38.2-61.8% of Wave 1) + breakout above Wave 1 high with surge in volume. The trade enters at the Wave 2 completion / Wave 3 beginning and targets the 1.618 Fibonacci extension of Wave 1. The inefficiency exists because Elliott Wave is typically applied on daily/weekly charts; the 1-min application captures institutional order flow waves that repeat 3-5 times per session.
mechanism: Institutional order flow arrives in bursts via algorithmic execution (TWAP/VWAP slicing), creating persistent directional pressure over 30-120 seconds. Retail and smaller participants follow the initial move, extending momentum before liquidity absorbs the flow and the order book rebalances.

indicators.name: wave1_detection
indicators.formula: impulse move > 15 bps within 5-10 bars, identified by zigzag(0.1%)

indicators.name: volume_surge_w3
indicators.formula: volume_1min / SMA(volume_1min, 20) at wave3 breakout bar

exit.signal_exit: RSI_14 reaches extreme (>80 for long, <20 for short) — wave3 likely exhausting

filters.vix_filter: India_VIX > 12 AND < 25 (need some vol for wave patterns but not chaotic)

weaknesses: Elliott Wave counting is inherently subjective — even the simplified version has ambiguity in identifying wave boundaries on noisy 1-min data.
The 0.382-0.618 retracement range for Wave 2 is wide. Many random pullbacks will qualify, generating false Wave 3 signals.
Wave 3 targets (1.618 extension) may not be reached intraday for lower-volatility stocks, causing frequent time-stop exits with partial gains.
prior_art: Elliott (1938) 'The Wave Principle'. Prechter & Frost (2001) 'Elliott Wave Principle'. Neely (1990) 'Mastering Elliott Wave'. In India, Elliott Wave is popular in technical analysis circles but systematic automated implementation is rare.
adaptation_notes: Converted from 1min to 5s bars. Lookback multiplier: 12x. Adaptations: timeframe scaling to 5-second candles; signal conversion from individual stock to NIFTY/BANKNIFTY index; lookback period scaling for 5-second bars. Stop/target calibrated for options point-based exits. Universe narrowed to NIFTY index.
